pins.name: D15
pins.label: D15 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: W6300 Ethernet chip interrupt (INTn / PIO_IRQ_PIN) - dedicated input line asserted by the onboard W6300 QSPI Ethernet controller to signal the RP2350, not general purpose. Confirmed via docs.wiznet.io W6300-EVB-Pico2 GPIO table and WIZnet-PICO-C firmware pin config (PIO_IRQ_PIN=15). See pfodWeb NOTE above re: the alias-collision gotcha.

pins.name: D16
pins.label: D16 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: W6300 Ethernet chip select (CSn) - dedicated output line from the RP2350 to the onboard W6300 QSPI Ethernet controller, not general purpose. pins_arduino.h declares PIN_SPI0_SS=16 (corrected from the plain-Pico2 template's MISO=16), so this pin auto-tags 'spi_ss' below, matching its real CSn function. Confirmed via docs.wiznet.io W6300-EVB-Pico2 GPIO table and WIZnet-PICO-C firmware pin config (PIN_CS=16). See pfodWeb NOTE above.

pins.name: GPIO25
pins.label: GPIO25 (Led active high)
pins.notes:
Connected to user LED (docs.wiznet.io W6300-EVB-Pico2 GPIO table: GPIO25 'Connected to user LED'). Not aliased at all by this board's inherited generic rp2350 pins_arduino.h (its common.h deliberately omits a D25 alias for the same reason PIN_LED itself is a bare #define, never turned into a static-const alias), so without this entry GPIO25 would not appear as a pin at all. Active-high assumed by the same standard Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico2 reference-design LED convention already confirmed and applied to this database's rpipico board.json (GPIO25 anode via series resistor to GPIO25, cathode to GND) - this board's vendor documentation states it 'works basically the same as a Raspberry Pi Pico board' with Ethernet added, and no inverted-LED wiring is documented anywhere. digital_input dropped to match this repo's established led_high precedent for dedicated onboard LED pins; pwm_output kept since arduino-pico's analogWrite() works on any RP2040/RP2350 GPIO.
